title: I built a zombie horde shooter in 3 days using AI, Phaser 4, Node.js and code-generated pixel art
author: Straight-Tea-8564
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I wanted to share a project I started just **3 days ago** that ended up growing much faster than I expected: **ZOMBRA**.

It’s a top-down pixel art zombie horde shooter inspired mainly by **Killing Floor** and **Left 4 Dead**, with some exploration and random loot while entering houses and abandoned locations.

What I find most interesting is the development process. I’ve been using AI heavily as a tool, mainly **Opus 5.5** for programming and building systems, **Suno** for the soundtrack, and almost all of the **pixel art is generated procedurally through code**, rather than using premade asset packs.

The game is being built with **Phaser 4**, and I’m using **Node.js** for the multiplayer side. I also built the website during these same three days.

So far the game already has zombie waves, survivor classes, weapons, a shop between waves, bosses, a bestiary, random events, building interiors, helicopter extraction and a survivor camp that I’m currently expanding into the main hub.

There’s obviously still a lot to polish, replace and improve, but I think it’s pretty crazy how far the project has come in only three days.

I’ve been developing games for a long time, and what surprised me is how much faster it lets me prototype systems, test ideas, iterate on visuals and throw away things that don’t work.

I plan to keep working on ZOMBRA and see how far I can take it.

**What do you guys think of the direction so far?**

If you want to follow the development or join the waitlist for future testing:

[**https://zombra.online/**](https://zombra.online/)

Would love to hear feedback, criticism and ideas from other devs.

comments.author: joshxor
comments.body: What prompts did you use for generating the pixel art?

replies.author: Straight-Tea-8564
replies.body: Good question. A lot of the art is generated procedurally in JavaScript, and I use AI to help write and refine those drawing routines. The palette, shapes and animations are defined in code, so there isn't one image-generation prompt behind the look. It's been an iterative process of adjusting things and testing them in the game.
